purpose: THE list of real boundaries. A worker stops and asks the owner when a rule here matches, and only then. Nothing else is a boundary: if it is not on this list, decide and proceed. No one reasons about what counts; add a rule here (one platform PR) when a new boundary is found. A repo may add its own rules in platform/boundaries.json (same format); it can add, never remove.
on_match: Stop that change. Put an ask on the work item (question, recommended action, due date, what happens if he does nothing, link) and work on something else.

rules.what: Anything that leaves the system toward a person or a company: sending an email or message, submitting a form, creating or changing an account or listing, buying, enrolling, publishing, uploading a manuscript.
Deleting data that cannot be rebuilt from git: a database, a table, a bucket, a volume, backups, the audit log, a recorder or Grist store.
Creating, revealing, changing or widening a credential, token, key or password of any account, or committing one.
Who may do what as root or on GitHub: sudoers, users and groups, SSH keys, the executor installer, repository or App permissions.
Firewall rules, router or DHCP settings, DNS upstreams, exposing a port or service beyond the LAN, Pi-hole allowlisting or removing a hand-made block.
Turning off the things that watch the system: the watchdog, the audit copy, FREEZE handling, the AI review, required checks, this boundary list.
Changing behaviour that acts on people, property or equipment while live (heating, locks, power, medication or health actions). Each repo lists its own paths in platform/boundaries.json.
